notes: nodeType is fully determined by the Python ast module's structural output: ast.parse(any_valid_expr_str, mode='exec') ALWAYS returns an ast.Module, so nodeType == 'Module' is always True at the first call to evaluate().
The predicate is therefore a structural tautology at the top-level entry point and is never re-entered during the recursive traversal (child nodes are Expr, BinOp, Compare, Name, Constant, etc.).
No os.environ keys, filesystem probes, hardware probes, or YAML keys influence the value of nodeType. It is derived entirely from the Python built-in type() applied to the ast.Module node.

The expressionStr (which ultimately determines the shape of the AST) is passed via addConstraint(). In the current codebase all call sites use hard-coded literals; there is no runtime injection path from CLI, YAML, env, or GPU probe.
If expressionStr were invalid Python syntax, ast.parse() would raise SyntaxError before evaluate() is ever called, so the predicate would not be evaluated at all.
